Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-1-prompt-long-0088", "row_sha256": "16e2d57aea03d0e4ec2799fc8a562abd5a22516b77cba48aeecb27124ab447b3", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "need a prompt for the atlas to cedar move for our field unit, but keep this as planning only, nobody should actually copy or move files from this prompt. we have fourteen completed field-study folders on the atlas shared drive and they need to go to the cedar shared drive when it is safe to plan that. they cover work from 2019 through 2023. the folder names and the preflight results are in the audit table i’ll supply with the prompt, so don’t make up folder names or say that any check passed before looking at that table. the key is a real condition, not a preference: only draft an ordered migration run sheet for moving those fourteen folders if every folder has both a passing checksum verification and a passing permission-mapping check. if that condition is not met, do not draft the move run sheet; instead make a discrepancy register showing which folder has which failed check. if all checks pass, use the run sheet path, not the register path. if not all checks pass, use the register path, not the run sheet path. return only the applicable one of those two things, no opening explanation and no second version.

these are the completed folders for the north coast field unit, not the live study workspace and not the general team drive. they hold final field-study materials such as interview transcripts, scanned consent records, observation notes, photo logs, and the write-ups that were filed with each study. some folders have all of those kinds of material and some have only a few; don’t assume each one has an identical contents list. their current top-level arrangement follows study and then year, and people use the folder names in the audit table when referring to the work. we want the prompt to keep that scope fixed at these fourteen completed folders. it should not quietly expand the request to other years, active work, or anything else on atlas just because it lives nearby. cedar is the intended destination, but this is still about what to prepare based on the checks, not about granting access or carrying out a transfer.

there are two checks that matter for the gate. one is whether the checksum verification passes for each of the fourteen folders. the other is whether the permission mapping passes for each folder, so the permissions represented for the atlas material have a corresponding mapping for cedar. all fourteen need a pass in both columns before the run sheet is the right output. one passing check by itself is not enough, and a pass for thirteen folders is not enough if the last folder fails either check. the audit table is the source for each folder’s name and the status of those two checks. i don’t want an invented judgment about what the statuses mean, or an overall “looks fine” conclusion that hides a row-level failure. please keep the gate tied to what the table says.

if the whole gate is satisfied, ask for an ordered run sheet for the move of the fourteen folders from atlas to cedar. it should be a planning document that a teammate could follow to understand the intended order and the folder names involved, but it must not claim the move has already happened. the proposed order should keep each study folder together rather than splitting its contents into separate transfers. the run sheet can refer to the existing study-and-year arrangement, because that is how people currently find the materials. don’t invent a detailed technical procedure or extra validation steps that aren’t in the supplied information; the point is to give an ordered plan based on the folder list and successful preflight checks. keep the source and destination names as atlas and cedar, respectively.

if the gate is not satisfied, the useful alternative is a discrepancy register instead of a migration run sheet. include the folder name from the audit table and identify whether its checksum verification failed, its permission mapping failed, or both, according to the table. show only actual failed checks; don’t turn a passing check into a problem and don’t guess why something failed. if several folders have issues, give each one its own entry so the affected work is clear. this branch is a report of the preflight discrepancies, not a proposal to move the folders anyway. the failed condition means no migration run sheet in that case, even if most folders have passed.

we have a note from the records coordinator that captures the concern behind the gate: “please leave the originals on atlas while we are still checking the destination permissions.” keep that as an ordinary quoted note if it helps explain the planning context, but don’t treat it as a separate result or imply that someone has already changed permissions. the prompt should distinguish the request to prepare one of the two outputs from actually performing the migration. no one is asking for the files to be copied, deleted, renamed, or shared as part of this task. don’t convert this into a recommendation to approve the move; the check results decide which output is applicable.

for clarity, use the following decision shape in the prompt:
1. all fourteen checksum checks and all fourteen permission-mapping checks pass: prepare only the ordered migration run sheet for the fourteen completed field-study folders.
2. otherwise: prepare only the discrepancy register, with the affected folder names and failed check types, and no run sheet.

keep the prompt focused on this one atlas-to-cedar episode. the table will supply the folder names and check statuses; the prompt should tell the person using it to rely on those entries rather than fill gaps from memory. retain the limitation that this is a planning task, and make the two branches easy to tell apart. output only the applicable artifact, with no introductory note, summary, or extra explanation. don't add a conclusion about whether the checks pass before the table has been reviewed.", "output": "Use the accompanying audit table to prepare one planning artifact for the North Coast Field Unit’s fourteen completed field-study folders on the Atlas shared drive, covering work from 2019 through 2023. The table supplies the folder names and the results of the two preflight checks. Do not invent folder names or assume that any check has passed. This request is for planning only: do not copy or move files, change permissions, or claim that a transfer has taken place.

Keep the scope to those fourteen completed folders. They are not the live study workspace or the general team drive. Their materials may include interview transcripts, scanned consent records, observation notes, photo logs, and filed study write-ups; contents vary between folders, so do not assume every folder contains the same items. The existing top-level arrangement is by study and then year. Atlas is the source and Cedar is the intended destination. Do not extend the request to other years, active work, or other material on Atlas.

Apply this gate using the audit table: prepare an ordered migration run sheet for moving the fourteen folders from Atlas to Cedar only if every folder has both a passing checksum verification and a passing permission-mapping check. A pass on only one check, or passes for only thirteen folders, does not satisfy the condition. Use the statuses shown in the table; do not hide a row-level failure behind an overall judgment. If all checks pass, use the run-sheet branch. Otherwise, use the discrepancy-register branch. Do not produce both.

1. If all fourteen checksum checks and all fourteen permission-mapping checks pass, prepare only an ordered migration run sheet for the fourteen completed folders. Use the folder names in the audit table and keep each study folder together rather than splitting its contents into separate transfers. The plan should make the intended order clear and may refer to the existing study-and-year arrangement. Do not invent a detailed technical procedure or additional validation steps that are not in the supplied information. The run sheet is a plan; it must not say that the move has already happened.

2. If either check fails for any folder, prepare only a discrepancy register. For each affected folder, use its name from the table and identify whether checksum verification failed, permission mapping failed, or both, as indicated there. Include only failed checks: do not describe a passing check as a problem or guess at the reason for a failure. Give separate entries where several folders have discrepancies. In this branch, do not provide a migration run sheet or propose moving the folders despite the failed condition.

The records coordinator’s note is: “please leave the originals on atlas while we are still checking the destination permissions.” Keep this as a quoted note if it helps explain the planning context. Do not present it as a check result or imply that permissions have already been changed. This task does not request copying, deleting, renaming, or sharing files, nor does it ask for a recommendation to approve the move. Let the audit results determine which single output is applicable.

Return only the applicable artifact: either the ordered migration run sheet or the discrepancy register. Include no introductory note, summary, or extra explanation. Do not state whether the checks pass until you have reviewed the audit table."}]
